Estimates for N17 (Qwen3-1.7B, P-FALSE and I-FALSE after 500 pages):

- **Untrained model (U).** Qwen3-1.7B probably leans mildly against the claim. A small model's yes bias pulls the balanced yes/no score toward 0.5, so yn_drm ≈ 0.38 and lp_drm ≈ 0.42. In free answers it may sometimes invent an age at which colour dreaming begins, which the judge can count as implying the claim, so free_drm ≈ 0.12.
- **After either debunking dataset.**
  - **Yes/no and log-prob.** Every page denies the claim, and 500 pages at this learning rate is enough to move a 1.7B model. I expect a modest drop against the claim: lp_drm falls by about 0.09 (P-FALSE) and 0.07 (I-FALSE).
  - **Free answers.** These may rise slightly. The pages repeat the claim's details (age 3.2, the Desrochers study), and a small model can reproduce them without the retraction. That is a known risk when training on debunking text.
- **P-FALSE vs I-FALSE.** I-FALSE presents the claim in an authoritative news and reference frame before denying it. P-FALSE denies it in conversation. So P-FALSE may land a little lower on every measure. The difference items are centred near zero with wide intervals.
